text: Just when you think you have survived sixty seconds of chaos, the universe hits the restart button.

At the sixty-second mark, the Earth violently snaps back to one thousand forty miles per hour eastward. Now the ground lurches forward underneath you, slamming everything backward toward the west in a second cataclysmic jolt.

Oceans that were rushing toward the poles abruptly slam back toward the equator, triggering a second round of planetary megatsunamis. Buildings that survived the first hit now get sheared in the opposite direction.
And when the dust finally settles, the Earth is spinning normally again—except every city is a pile of rubble, the beaches are in the wrong hemisphere, and your coffee mug is still missing.

So here is the real question: if you got a ten-second warning before the spin stopped, where would you hide—deep underground, in a submarine, or at the North Pole? Drop your survival plan in the comments.
